title: Asking for Directions
summary: A tourist asks a passer-by how to get to the train station and follows the instructions step by step.
description: A short elementary dialogue focusing on prepositions of place (next to, opposite, on the corner of) and basic imperative forms for giving directions.

vocabulary.definition: go in the direction of your left side
go in the direction of your right side
continue in the same direction, without turning
on the other side of the street, facing it

dialogue.text: Excuse me, can you help me? I am looking for the train station.
Of course. The station is not far from here.
Great. How do I get there?
Go straight ahead for two blocks. Then turn left at the traffic lights.
Left at the traffic lights. Okay.
Walk past the bank and turn right on the corner of King Street.
Right on King Street. Is the station opposite the park?
Yes, exactly. It is a big building with a clock on top.
You are welcome. Have a good day.

questions.q: Where does the tourist want to go?
What does the tourist do at the traffic lights?

trueFalse.statement: The station is far from where the tourist is.
trueFalse.explanation: The passer-by says 'The station is not far from here.'

trueFalse.statement: The tourist turns right on King Street.
trueFalse.explanation: The passer-by says 'turn right on the corner of King Street.'

teacherTips: Draw a simple map of three streets on the board before listening. Students follow the route with their finger as they listen.
Teach the difference between 'turn left' and 'turn right' with a quick TPR activity before pressing play.
Extension: students write their own directions between two places in their town and swap with a partner.

es.title: Pedir indicaciones
es.summary: Un turista pregunta a un transeúnte cómo llegar a la estación de tren y sigue las instrucciones paso a paso.
es.description: Un diálogo elemental centrado en preposiciones de lugar (next to, opposite, on the corner of) y la forma imperativa básica para dar indicaciones.

vocabulary.definition: ir en la dirección de tu lado izquierdo
ir en la dirección de tu lado derecho
continuar en la misma dirección, sin girar
al otro lado de la calle, frente a ella

questions.q: ¿Qué hace el turista en el semáforo?

trueFalse.statement: La estación está lejos del turista.
trueFalse.explanation: El transeúnte dice 'The station is not far from here'.

trueFalse.statement: El turista gira a la derecha en King Street.
trueFalse.explanation: El transeúnte dice 'turn right on the corner of King Street'.

teacherTips: Dibuja un mapa sencillo de tres calles en la pizarra antes de escuchar. Los estudiantes siguen la ruta con el dedo mientras escuchan.
Enseña la diferencia entre 'turn left' y 'turn right' con una actividad TPR rápida antes de reproducir el audio.
Ampliación: los estudiantes escriben sus propias indicaciones entre dos lugares de su ciudad y las intercambian con un compañero.
